text:
maria_support: ACME says our internal API (api.internal.acme) started returning NXDOMAIN from some EU hosts after yesterday's VPC peering change. Anyone seen this pattern? @josh_infra

josh_infra: Seen similar. quick check: which resolver IPs are the failing hosts using?

maria_support: They show 10.0.0.2 (VPC resolver) on host-a, 10.1.0.2 (shared resolver) on host-b. dig outputs: `dig +short api.internal.acme @10.0.0.2` -> (blank) + status: NXDOMAIN. `dig +short api.internal.acme @10.1.0.2` -> 10.2.3.4

nora_netops: Possible: two private hosted zones for acme.internal in different accounts + overlapping VPC associations. Route53 split-horizon can return different answers depending on which hosted zone is associated with the resolver context.

maria_support: We ran `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name acme.internal` — shows two zones (Z1PROD in prod-account, Z2SHRD in shared-sandbox). Z2SHRD was accidentally associated with prod-vpc during a CFN change.

josh_infra: Can we confirm resolver rule precedence and any conditional forwarders? Also check VPC associations: I usually run `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id Z2SHRD` and `aws ec2 describe-vpcs --filters Name=tag:Stack,Values=*` to correlate.

nora_netops: Also check Route53 Resolver rules and associations. Example commands:
```
aws route53resolver list-resolver-rules
aws route53resolver list-resolver-rule-associations --resolver-rule-id <id>
```
Those will show forwarding rules that can change resolution behavior across accounts.

maria_support: Customer confirms they have an outbound resolver rule pointing to shared-account resolvers and we have inbound endpoint in prod. I think the CFN run associated the shared hosted zone to prod-vpc and resolver cached NXDOMAIN. TTL is 30s but we saw flapping for a few minutes.

josh_infra: Cache could be the culprit. Try `dig +norecurse @10.0.0.2 api.internal.acme` to hit the authoritative resolver directly. If authoritative differs, disassociate the wrong hosted zone.

maria_support: Repro steps for infra to validate from prod side:
1) From prod host: `dig +short api.internal.acme @10.0.0.2` -> NXDOMAIN
2) From same host: `dig +short api.internal.acme @10.1.0.2` -> 10.2.3.4
3) `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id Z2SHRD` shows association with VPC `vpc-0badass` (prod)
4) Disassociate Z2SHRD from prod-vpc -> resolves immediately (we verified).

nora_netops: Suggested fix: remove accidental association, run `route53resolver test-dns-answer` from the VPC to validate end-to-end, and add CFN guardrail to prevent creating duplicate private zones for the same name. Also add alert when multiple hosted zones share the same private name.

deploy-bot: deploy completed: disassociated Z2SHRD from vpc-0badass at 1946689290

sam_acme: Confirmed — looks good on our side, api resolves consistently now, thanks.

maria_support: :thumbsup: Confirmed with customer too. Marking resolved, will follow up with postmortem and CFN fix.
